venue: Ben Hill Griffin Stadium, Gainesville FL
title: Week 1 vs FAU
dek: Faulkner keeps FAU from sitting on Baugh. White keeps FAU from knowing who has the edge. FAU still moved the chains on the short throw Florida left open.
watchNote: PROVISIONAL — combined condensed tape + GNFP Week 2. Fan rail stays empty until Charles approves.
headline: Baugh is the night. Faulkner’s job is to keep you from putting extra men on him. Woods is how White messes with the tackle.

offense.body:
Buster Faulkner’s whole night is one job: do not let FAU decide in advance that the ball is going to Jadan Baugh.

If they do, they put extra bodies near the line and Baugh is done. So Faulkner keeps changing who is where, and what the line is selling, until FAU is guessing. Same start. Different answer. They can still go the other way without changing the play.

Here is what that looked like.

FAU is scared of Baugh, so they keep extra defenders close to him. That leaves Vernell Brown III with grass. Philo throws him a short ball. First man misses. Brown runs 49 yards and scores. People will remember a long touchdown. It was a short throw and a missed tackle. That is Faulkner: you came up for the run, he threw the easy one behind you.

The next trick is the fake run. Two tackles look like they are pulling to lead a run. FAU steps with those tackles. The ball goes the other way — to Brown, with the three interior linemen already out in front of him. Later it is Duke Clark, same idea, and those big people are already down the field when he scores from 10. You followed the fake. The ball went where you left.

If FAU does not bite — if they stay put and play Baugh — he runs it anyway. He scores from 12 with those same pulling linemen actually leading him this time. In the third quarter everybody in the Swamp knows it is Baugh, and he still goes 61. Fourteen carries, 160 yards, three rushing scores. There were snaps FAU called the run blitz, filled every hole, and he still ripped it. That is not Faulkner winning those snaps. That is Baugh. Faulkner’s job is to keep you from putting eleven men on him so those snaps stay fair.

He also lines the receivers way out wide, and sometimes he puts Brown and Wilson one behind the other on that side. Now FAU has a bad choice. Crowd Baugh, and Brown or Wilson is one-on-one with half the field. Spread out to cover those two, and Baugh is running against fewer people. That is why Brown’s night was not a gadget night — the short throw, the screen, the 14, the 33. They kept using the space FAU gave them.

Sometimes Florida puts more players on one side of the field, then motions a man across right before the snap. FAU is still counting. Florida can still go the other way. Their numbers were late all night.

One more look they will keep using: the tackle who is supposed to block the pass rusher instead takes off the other way, like it is a run. The rusher has to choose. Chase Philo, or honor the fake. Week one they showed that a lot and did not cash it much. They will hand the ball off from that same look. Remember it when you see it.

Pistol — Philo with Baugh behind him — showed up once early. They ran it, then they faked it and Wilson sat down in the hole in coverage for 19. That was one look. It is not who they are. Wilson moved the chains all night because he sits in the empty grass they leave him.

Philo ran the building. He got them lined up. He snapped it with time on the clock. When they rushed him he kept his eyes downfield, stepped up, and still found somebody. He does not have to be the star. Stockton caught a ball that was a little late and still walked it in from the 11. Abrams’ 63 was the deep one when FAU finally crowded Baugh — the line looked like pass, not run, and Philo threw it over the top. Lead Abrams a step and he walks in. The interception is Micah Mays. The ball came off his hands. Sweeney was sitting there. When Philo holds it, the play dies.

The line is not blowing people off the ball. They are clean — almost no penalties, and the late defensive-line shift that wrecked them last year did not get them. They are also not arriving at the second level fast. The wide sweep they tried, they cannot run yet. Faulkner still shows it so FAU has to respect the edge. What he does instead: he does not ask this line to block everybody. He leaves people unblocked on purpose and lets Baugh and the fakes do the rest.

The snaps over Philo’s head are a technique thing. Sumrall already said it: a certain run block messes with Harrison Moore’s hands. The one that lost twenty yards inside the five is the one that can lose a real game. The other miss: Philo kept it, FAU’s end was still there, minus two. The idea was fine. They lost the play.

Late, they block down the field like they mean it. Ten-yard runs become thirty. Micah Jones blows up one man, then the next, and they throw him the last touchdown. That is not a coincidence. Same idea as Clark’s score: get a big person in front of a skill player.

What Saturday was: a coordinator who will not let you sit on Baugh, a back you cannot tackle if the box is honest, and a quarterback who ran the operation. What to clean is the snap, the keep they lost, and the ball off Mays.
bullets: You come up for Baugh, he throws the short one to Brown. That is the 49.
You follow the fake run, the ball goes the other way — Brown, later Clark.
You play it straight, Baugh runs it. The 12 and the 61.
Clean the snap, the keep they lost, and the ball off Mays.

defense.body:
FAU wants to throw it short until you come up and take that throw away. Florida never took it away.

The corners played soft. The linebackers did not step into the short area. FAU saw that before the snap, and then they got that throw anyway. Ninety snaps. At one point they were 10-of-13 on third down. Henry and Valsin just kept catching the five-to-eight yard ball. Sumrall said it Monday: third-and-1, you cannot have your corner nine yards off. That happened. White will live with the short throw if Florida tackles. They did not tackle enough of it, and nobody was standing where that ball lands, so it became a long night.

He still has a real idea. He moves Jayden Woods so FAU’s tackle cannot get comfortable. Sometimes Woods is the man on the edge. Sometimes he walks inside and somebody else has that edge. Mix it. Often. Do not leave him in one spot all night, and do not leave him on an island if he starts chasing.

When Veltkamp holds the ball, that idea pays. Coleman sells the middle of the field, the ball goes outside, and Coleman is already there. That interception is a bait. Not a blitz. He moved the quarterback’s eyes. He tips the next one. Dijon Johnson goes up and gets it. Same idea. Bett later beats the quarterback at the 1, the ball comes out, Johnson falls on it. McCloud stops them on fourth-and-2. The safeties were the part that looked like a staff — Coleman and Thornton. Kanye Clark played a real night in the slot and lost one fade with no help over the top. That fade is the other side of playing soft. Valsin, 20 yards, touchdown. Same play Stockton ran the other way.

What they lost are the jobs inside the plan. The pile at the 1 — they had enough people, they lost the yard. Veltkamp walking in from 7 because the edge left. Woods is the guy who is supposed to keep that edge. When he chases, FAU ran at him. Later in the game Florida rushed four and still played the corners soft. That takes away the deep ball. That also leaves the short throw and the fade alive.

They were ready for the tempo. They were not still looking at the sideline when FAU snapped it. Veltkamp is a real quarterback — he can throw it and he can run it. Sumrall called the defense atrocious at times because ninety snaps and those fourth downs are what you get when the short throw is free.

Next week: stand where that short ball lands. Keep Woods on the edge when the quarterback keeps it. Make him hold it. Coleman already showed you what that looks like.
bullets: The short throw was open. That is why FAU ran 90 snaps.
White moves Woods so the tackle cannot get comfortable.
When Veltkamp holds it, Coleman and Johnson take it.
Fix the pile, the edge, and the fade.

specials.body: The drive stalls. They take the points. Durkin from 53. Florida never punts. FAU’s 18-yard punt is how the second Florida score starts.
bullets: FAU’s 18-yard punt sets up the short field.

nextWeek.look: Campbell will throw it short and the quarterback will run it. Sixkiller is their guy. Florida will still hand it to Baugh and keep changing the picture. White has to stand on that short throw and keep Woods on the edge when Sixkiller pulls it.
